title: POC weekly - latency tuning sync
topics: KV cache hit rate and prefix caching
next_steps: Redwood to share updated latency runbook and p95/p99 charts
BlueHarbor to provide 50 real-world prompts + sequence length histogram
SE to run kernel-choice benchmark (q4_K vs q3/float16) and share results
Schedule deep kernel/ROCm tuning session next week
action_items: Lena Park: Send updated latency runbook and consolidated benchmark slides (due 2026-07-23)
Owen Brooks: Upload 50 sample prompts and seq length distribution to shared spreadsheet (due 2026-07-23)
Marco Diaz: Re-run kernel-selection benchmark with q4_K and fp16 fallbacks and include streaming TTFT (due 2026-07-24)
Sasha Kim: Confirm acceptable p50/p95 targets for TTFT and streaming (due 2026-07-22)
transcript:
00:00 Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we have about 45 minutes, agenda is quick review of the runs from last week and decide next tuning steps.
00:12 Sasha Kim: Yep thanks, we pushed the stress test overnight. saw some interesting numbers, p50 looks okay but p95 is spiking on long sequences.
00:28 Marco Diaz: Quick context — we ran two paths: streaming enabled on the redwood-hosted endpoint and non-streaming for the dedicated node. model variants were the redwood-7b-rlhf-ish and a quantized q4_K build, though the naming in the logs might be off.
00:45 Owen Brooks: I noticed when sequence length > 1024 tail latency jumps a lot, is that KV cache behaving?
00:53 Marco Diaz: Yeah, probable KV cache thrashing — when prefixes vary we lose cache hits and kernel choices matter. we also saw higher kernel fallback rates on the ROCm boxes.
01:10 Priya Rao: Real quick — baseline targets from our side: TTFT p50 under 120ms, p95 under 400ms for typical prompts (avg seq 280). streaming should be sub-200ms first token if possible.
01:28 Lena Park: Good clarity. On our last runs, TTFT (non-streaming cold) was around 180ms p50 and 520ms p95 for one-off requests on the hosted pool, streaming first token was ~160ms p50 but p95 closer to 450ms on longer sequences.
01:45 Sasha Kim: That matches some of what we saw. can we break down what contributed to that 520 p95? is it batching, kernel selection, or infra noise?
02:02 Marco Diaz: Short answer: a combination. We saw heavy variance from autoscaling warm-up (container cold starts), plus fallback to a slower kernel path for certain sequence lengths. When batch size got above 8 we observed queueing adding 50-100ms per request.
02:20 Owen Brooks: The test used default batching policy — can we try smaller max batch and higher concurrency to see tradeoffs?
02:28 Marco Diaz: Absolutely, we recommended in the notes to try max_batch 4 with aggressive batching timeout 7ms, and to enable prefix KV caching for repeated prompt families.
02:44 Priya Rao: Also curious about quantization impact — q4_K vs q3 or fp16? any big regression on TTFT?
02:52 Marco Diaz: q4_K saves memory and sometimes reduces token latency because of cache size, but kernel availability matters. In some GPUs the q4 kernel path isn't optimized, causing fallback to slower kernels — that's where we saw the p95 tail. fp16 generally more consistent but higher mem.
03:10 Sasha Kim: So step would be run per-kernel benchmarks and also capture seq-length distribution; we can then pick a quant/profile that fits our seq histogram.
03:22 Marco Diaz: Exactly. we ran an ad-hoc kernel sweep yesterday: q4_K on cuda box had p50 TTFT 145ms p95 480ms; fp16 was p50 170ms p95 430ms. results vary by hardware, and streaming first token differed by ~20-30ms.
03:40 Owen Brooks: Are those numbers from the dedicated nodes or hosted pool?
03:45 Marco Diaz: Hosted pool for the q4_K numbers; dedicated node fp16 numbers were from an A100-based private cluster. remember some of the naming in the run logs had typos — the exporter labeled one run redwood-rt-7b which is actually our 7b-optim variant.
04:02 Lena Park: That's fine, these exporters are messy. main point: for BlueHarbor, given your seq histogram with many short prompts but some long tails, we might recommend streaming for short prompts and a non-streaming dedicated route for long completions, plus smart routing.
04:18 Sasha Kim: Smart routing sounds good. do you have an automated fallback if the dedicated node is saturated?
04:24 Marco Diaz: Yes, we can set policy to route overflow to hosted with a cheaper model variant and use output-quality regression checks. fallback adds latency but maintains availability.
04:36 Priya Rao: One concern from infra: we run everything in customer VPC, do the kernel optimizations depend on custom drivers?
04:44 Marco Diaz: For private deployment we do need compatible CUDA/ROCm drivers, and some optimized kernels require specific driver versions. We'll share a matrix.
04:52 Owen Brooks: On the autoscaling cold starts, can we pre-warm KV cache or keep a small reserved hot pool?
04:58 Marco Diaz: Yes — keep a small reserved capacity and use prefix caching to mitigate cold starts. that reduces cold TTFT significantly — in our tests reserved hot pool cut p95 by ~130ms on average.
05:15 Sasha Kim: Nice. for the kernel benchmarks, can you include streaming TTFT separately from steady-state token latency?
05:22 Marco Diaz: Absolutely, we'll split metrics: first-token-time, token-throughput, p50/p95 for both streaming and non-streaming.
05:30 Lena Park: quick question — are there any security concerns in sharing the sample prompts?
05:34 Sasha Kim: They have PII redacted, so should be fine. we'll scrub and share.
05:40 Lena Park: Great. I'll send the shared spreadsheet link after this call.
05:44 Owen Brooks: Another item — we saw some variance during peak hours in our cluster, likely due to noisy neighbor VM scheduling. can we recommend instance sizing?
05:53 Marco Diaz: We suggest reserved dedicated slices for predictable throughput; e.g., for your 50 rps target with avg seq 300, we'd size for sustained concurrency of 20 across A100s or equivalent. we'll include a capacity calc.
06:12 Sasha Kim: Would kernel tuning affect cost? like if q4_K reduces memory, can we pack more models and lower cost?
06:19 Marco Diaz: Yes — quantization helps unit economics. if kernel support is good we can reduce nodes; but need to validate p95 impact. Redwood Optimize can simulate cost/perf tradeoffs — we'll share the Optimize config used.
06:34 Priya Rao: Any quick wins we can do this week?
06:38 Marco Diaz: Sure: 1) enable prefix KV caching for repeat prompts, 2) change max_batch to 4 and batching timeout to 7ms in the staging route, 3) pin the model to the fp16 variant for dedicated route as a control.
06:52 Owen Brooks: We'll try those and run the same stress script.
06:55 Lena Park: I'll drop the runbook and config snippets. Marco will re-run kernel benchmarks. Sasha will confirm target SLOs.
07:02 Sasha Kim: Targets: TTFT p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 400ms; streaming first token p50 <= 150ms p95 <= 350ms — we'll confirm but that's our goal.
07:20 Marco Diaz: Noted. question — did BlueHarbor want us to include regression alerts tied to prompt sets?
07:26 Sasha Kim: Yes, we want to be alerted if quality drops when switching quantized model.
07:31 Lena Park: We can wire up eval hooks in the Console to monitor unit-quality on the pilot prompts.
07:36 Priya Rao: Good. slight tangent — procurement asked about dedicated pricing if we go into reserved capacity next quarter.
07:44 Lena Park: I'll have pricing ranges in the follow-up doc, plus a committed tier estimate.
07:49 Owen Brooks: Any competitors we should be aware of? we ran a quick comparison with Anthropic's hosted infra; they had lower p50 but similar tails.
07:58 Marco Diaz: Right — different infra tradeoffs. Anthropic had optimized streaming stack, OpenAI strong for short TTFT but expensive at scale. Replicate and Vertex are more DIY.
08:12 Sasha Kim: Alright let's recap quickly.
08:15 Lena Park: Recap: Marco to run kernel sweep (q4_K vs fp16) and include streaming TTFT; Owen to upload 50 sample prompts + seq histogram; Lena to send runbook, capacity calc, and pricing ranges; Sasha to confirm SLOs. we'll aim to have results mid next week.
08:35 Priya Rao: Sounds good. one more small ask — can you include the exact driver/kernel matrix needed for private deployment?
08:42 Marco Diaz: Yes we'll add the driver matrix to the runbook.
08:46 Lena Park: Great thanks all, we'll follow up with docs. end of call.
45:00 [call ended]
